deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X smooth (or 'differentially flat') over S. M^. is a differential complex, i.e. O_S-linear differential operators between O_X-modules. Q^*[M^.] is the bicomplex obtained by linearizing M^. along the infinitesimal neighbourhoods X^{[n]} of the diagonal. Q^0[M^.] is essentially P^infinity_{X/S} (x) M^., with linearized differentials. It carries a natural stratification relative to S. The previous page establishes that the V^q = H^q(Q^0[M^.]) are O_X-modules (via the left structure) with natural stratifications. Taking cohomology of the bicomplex in the M^.-direction yields the 'de Rham/Cech' complexes C^.(V^q) attached to these stratifications.

This page states the resulting spectral sequence, the spectral sequence of the bicomplex with respect to the second filtration:
  H^*(X, M^.) = H^*(X, Q^*[M^.]) <= E_2^{pq} = H^p(X, C^.(V^q)).
The first isomorphism holds because M^. -> Q^*[M^.] is a quasi-isomorphism (a formal Poincare lemma / linearization resolution). Grothendieck flags the need to check this against EGA 0_III (hypercohomology spectral sequences).

He then defines the cohomology of a stratified module V relative to S as
  H^p_str(X, V) := H^p(X, C^._str(V)).
This is the hypercohomology of the canonical complex attached to the stratification, a precursor of infinitesimal/stratifying-site cohomology. The spectral sequence is rewritten (boxed) as
  H^*(X, M^.) <= E_2^{pq} = H^p_str(X, V^q(M^.)), with V^q(M^.) = H^q(Q^0[M^.]).

Corollary: if V^q(M^.) = 0 for q != q0, then H^n(X, M^.) = H^{n-q0}_str(X, V^{q0}(M^.)). Say q0 = 0, so M^. is a 'differential resolution' of the stratified module V = V^0. The hypercohomology of M^. then depends only on V, not on the chosen differential complex resolving it (completed on the next page).

The goal: show that de Rham cohomology (the next page takes M^. = Omega^._{X/S} (x) V, which is a differential resolution of V in characteristic 0 by the formal Poincare lemma) computes an intrinsic cohomology of the stratified module. This is the core of the comparison 'de Rham = infinitesimal (crystalline) cohomology in char 0' in the 1968 Crystals lectures.
errors: Not an error but a gap: the identification of the E_1 terms of the bicomplex with the complexes C^.(V^q), hence the E_2 description, relies on the flatness hypotheses of the previous page (flatness of Q^0[M^.] and of P^n over O_X, which needs X/S smooth or 'differentially flat'). These are only gestured at ('critère: dégager').

Convergence of the spectral sequence needs boundedness assumptions (M^. bounded below, finite cohomological dimension or a first-quadrant bicomplex). These are not stated; Grothendieck himself marks 'vérif à EGA 0_III ?'.
Notation is unsettled: the hypercohomology symbol vs H_str, and an 'X_str' subscript with 'str' crossed out, show the definition of stratified cohomology was still being fixed.

ideas.what: Linearization of a differential complex M^. into a bicomplex Q^*[M^.] of stratified (crystal-like) modules, with M^. quasi-isomorphic to its linearization.
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of differential operators, L(M^.) = P^infinity (x) M^.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals, IHES 1968); developed by Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974) and Berthelot-Ogus (1978)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (notes by Coates-Jussila, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968)

ideas.what: Cohomology of a stratified module defined as hypercohomology of the canonical complex C^._str(V) attached to the stratification.
ideas.modern_name: Stratifying/infinitesimal cohomology of a stratified module (cohomology on the infinitesimal or stratifying site)

ideas.what: Spectral sequence H^p_str(X, H^q(Q^0[M^.])) => H^{p+q}(X, M^.), and the corollary that a differential resolution of a stratified module V computes H_str(V) independently of the resolution.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of de Rham / differential-complex cohomology with infinitesimal cohomology; independence of the differential resolution
ideas.where_published: Crystals (Dix exposés); cf. Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline, linearization chapters

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the standard linearization argument and spectral sequence that appear in Grothendieck's 1968 'Crystals' lectures and were systematized by Berthelot. It is of historical interest as a working draft (notation for stratified cohomology still unsettled, EGA check flagged), but there is no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: In the boxed formula, the image reads V^q(M^.) = H^q(Q^0[M^.]) (with Q^0, i.e. Q°), not Q^.[M^.].

The last line likely reads 'Ceci montre, supposant p.ex. que q0=0, que le premier membre ...' ('la première ms' is probably 'le premier membre'), continuing on the next page with 'ne dépend que du Module stratifié'.
In the boxed spectral sequence, 'str' is written (and partly crossed out) under H^p, with a possible subscript on X; the reading H^p_str(X, V^q(M^.)) is the intended sense.
In the second line, the phrase after '(vérif à EGA 0_III ?).' seems to be something like '... pour abréger l'écriture, on prend la définition ...'; the 'Comme[?] comme[?]' reading is doubtful.
